claims.text: Surface segregation of Cu governs the onset and progression of premelting and melting in initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu is the low-melting component of the FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticle system.
Segregated Cu nucleates a disordered, Cu-rich liquid surface layer.
Formation of the Cu-rich liquid surface layer lowers the effective melting-onset temperature.
Inert-gas condensation produces initially solid and homogeneous equiatomic FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
The nanoparticles considered are typically smaller than 50 nm.
An ultrathin inert oxide or refractory nitride coating can inhibit Cu migration and surface segregation.
Cu accumulation at the nanoparticle surface creates a region with a lower local melting temperature than the particle interior.
Increasing temperature causes relatively mobile Cu atoms to migrate toward the nanoparticle surface.
The Cu-enriched surface initiates surface premelting.
The premolten surface layer coalesces and promotes complete particle melting.
Suppressing Cu migration delays surface premelting and raises the apparent melting temperature.
Relative to uncoated particles, passivated particles will have higher onset temperatures for both premelting and complete melting.
Passivated particles will show reduced surface Cu enrichment and delayed morphological changes during heating.
Uncoated FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles naturally permit Cu segregation at elevated temperatures.
The proposed mechanism applies primarily to particles below approximately 50 nm, while larger particles may exhibit different kinetics and diffusion lengths.
Statistically indistinguishable melting onsets together with similar surface Cu profiles in passivated and uncoated particles would falsify the proposed Cu-segregation mechanism.
